meta.source: Copernicus Emergency Management Service, European Drought Observatory
meta.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information 2026
meta.cadenceNote: The CDI is published once every ten days. A reading two or three weeks old is the newest there is, not a stale one.

classes.label: less rain than normal
classes.detail: A precipitation deficit, measured against this place’s own record.

classes.label: dry ground
classes.detail: The precipitation deficit has reached the soil: soil moisture is below normal.

classes.label: vegetation under stress
classes.detail: Plant growth is below normal, together with the dry ground and the missing rain.

classes.label: recovered
classes.detail: Rain, soil water and plant growth have returned to normal after a dry episode.

classes.label: soil recovering
classes.detail: Soil moisture is back above its threshold, but the dry episode is not closed.

classes.label: vegetation recovering
classes.detail: Plant growth is back above its threshold, but the dry episode is not closed.
